# LiFePO4 vs NMC: LiFePO4 is the better pick for most people

LiFePO4 (also called LFP) is the better buy for nearly everyone. NMC mainly makes sense for a small, light unit you'll use rarely.

## Where LiFePO4 wins

- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. Same-maker pairs show it clearly: Jackery's Explorer 1000 (NMC) is rated for 500 cycles to 70%, while the 1000 v2 (LFP) is rated for 4,000 to 70% ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). One full cycle a day, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 lasts about 8 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells ran cooler and less violently when they failed. One test peaked at 259°C for LFP vs 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). This is a real plus for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Cost over time:** Price per Wh is now lower for LFP (median $0.55 vs $0.95 in one dataset), and cost per rated cycle is much lower ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Availability:** Most current models are LFP. NMC survives mainly in small compacts and older stock.

## Where NMC wins

- **Energy density:** NMC cells store more energy per pound, but the gap shrinks a lot in finished stations. In one database the median was only about 10% more Wh per pound for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)), and some LFP units are lighter per Wh than NMC ones ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare specific models rather than assuming.

## Caveats

- LFP isn't fireproof. It also reached thermal runaway earlier in one overcharge test, though the failure was milder ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- Cold weather depends more on the maker than the chemistry. Most stations of both types won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- Cycle ratings aren't uniform. Some are "to 80%" and some "to 70%", and test conditions differ ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- The sources disagree on typical NMC cycle life (500 to 2,000), so treat exact numbers loosely. The direction is the same everywhere.
- If you already own a working NMC unit, keep using it. For occasional outage backup, either chemistry's cycle count will outlast the battery's calendar life.

## An LFP example to consider

The **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating (to 80%) and a 5-year warranty. It isn't expandable and weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb). It lists at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the source says it tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-24 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)).

[Buy at BLUETTI's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Checkout has the final say on price.

Whichever you choose, size the unit for what you'll run first, and chemistry second.
